messages:
Maya: Quick sync — I'm drafting the RFC for customer-managed rate policies in Private/VPC. TL;DR: tenants upload a policy blob to their control plane; we validate + distribute to local dataplane enforcers. Need alignment on enforcement model (central vs local), per-key vs per-org granularity, and UI/validation UX.
Alex: I like local enforcement for latency but worried about eventual consistency when policy changes roll out during spikes.
Sasha: Agree with Alex. Local token-bucket on each proxy, with a control-plane push + versioned policies. If we include a short TTL for overrides we can avoid long tail inconsistencies.
Kevin: One requirement: allow customers to opt into burst windows (e.g., short high QPS). Need explicit fields in the policy for burst_capacity and cooldown.
Irene: From infra side: how do we handle replay/duplicate requests when enforcement is distributed? We can't rely on a single global counter unless we want p99 latency hit.
John: Practical idea: per-key token-bucket sharded by tenant id + key hash, use locally-consumed burst tokens and periodic reconciliation with control plane metrics. On mismatch, control plane can mark a key as degraded and fallback to conservative limit.
Maya: +1. UX question: console should show policy diff, last-applied version, and a dry-run mode that simulates enforcement against recent traffic. Also audit logs + signed policy digest (for compliance).
Alex: Sample minimal policy schema sketch:
```
{
  "version": "1",
  "scope": "api_key", // api_key | org
  "limits": {
    "rate_per_minute": 6000,
    "burst_capacity": 1200,
    "cooldown_seconds": 60
  },
  "fallback": "throttle" // throttle | queue | allow
}
```
Sasha: We should support nested rules: route-level overrides and client-specific exceptions. But we must cap complexity to keep validation robust.
Kevin: For Private customers we must let them host policy blobs in their S3/Vault and reference via signed URL + KMS signature. We can't store plaintext policies for air-gapped customers.
Irene: Telemetry: each local enforcer emits per-key counters and a policy_version tag. Control plane aggregates for rollouts and creates alerts when a rollout causes >5% 429 increase.
John: Ops note: add a global safety valve on control plane that can remotely disable customer-managed policies (revert to platform defaults) in case of cascade failures.
Maya: Implementation plan proposal: phase 1 = read-only policy upload + validation + dry-run in console; phase 2 = local enforcement with push & reconciliation; phase 3 = advanced features (route-level rules, signed remote policy store).
Alex: Deployment concerns: can we gate phase2 behind a feature flag per-customer? If so, we'll need migration steps for Dedicated pools and Private clusters.
Sasha: We'll also want an API endpoint for CI to programmatically validate and upload policies + a webhook for policy-change events.
Maya: Great. Action items: Alex/Irene draft dataplane contract for token-bucket + reconciliation (due EOW). Sasha to prototype console dry-run UX. Kevin to write security constraints for signed policy stores. John to add emergency rollback hook to control plane. I'll collate into RFC draft tomorrow.
